requirements.requirement: Provide a working IMAP service on node1 that node2 can access.
requirements.summary: Node1 runs enabled, active Dovecot with IMAPS permitted through the firewall. Node2 directly authenticated, selected INBOX, and retrieved two messages both before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Use a dedicated archive account and demonstration password.
requirements.summary: A dedicated non-login archive account was created with a randomly generated credential, and node2 successfully authenticated as that account over TLS.

requirements.requirement: Make both messages retrievable while preserving their Message-ID values, bodies, and mailbox.tsv read/unread state.
requirements.summary: Remote read-only IMAP retrieval showed exactly two messages: <one@branch.test> with body “Shipment arrived.” and the Seen flag, and <two@branch.test> with body “Shipment departed.” without Seen. The working files also matched the staged messages byte-for-byte.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supplied staged mailbox intact.
requirements.summary: Final node1 hashes for mailbox.tsv and both staged messages exactly match the preparation baseline, while separate working copies were used by Dovecot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. Dovecot 2.3.16 was installed from the RHEL 9 AppStream repository, and final package-health checks passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and remote behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, network, service, mailbox, authentication, and retrieval behavior.
limitations: Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, account and credential creation, the separate working Maildir, Dovecot configuration, firewall/service enablement, persistent SELinux labeling, and both protocol-required reboots all had direct task or verification roles. The initial unsuccessful read-only IMAP check exposed the SELinux labeling issue and was followed by the necessary persistent correction. Final lifecycle observations show healthy package state and no failed services on either node; the added listeners belong to the requested IMAP service.
